primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease due to diabetic‑hypertensive nephropathy
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (CKD assessment and management) and NG107 (Renal replacement therapy and conservative management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to target BP <130/80 mmHg (max 10 mg daily)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and if liver enzymes rise
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 statin for all CKD patients

medications.dose: 10,000 IU sub‑cutaneously once weekly (dose titrated to maintain Hb 100‑120 g/L)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 100‑120 g/L, then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107 ESA for CKD anaemia (Hb <100 g/L) after confirming iron stores

medications.dose: 1000 mg IV over 15 min (single infusion; repeat if ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20%)
medications.duration: Single infusion; repeat based on iron studies
medications.purpose: Replete iron stores before ESA therapy
medications.nice_justification: NG107 IV iron for iron‑deficiency in CKD

medications.dose: 800 mg chewable tablet with each main meal (TID), titrate to achieve phosphate <1.5 mmol/L
medications.duration: Until phosphate <1.5 mmol/L, then review every 3‑6 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107 phosphate binder for CKD hyperphosphataemia

medications.dose: 0.25 µg orally once daily (adjust according to calcium & PTH)
medications.duration: Until calcium and PTH within target, then review every 3‑6 months
medications.purpose: Manage secondary hyperparathyroidism / vitamin D deficiency
medications.nice_justification: NG107 vitamin D analogue for CKD‑related SHPT

medications.dose: 500 mg orally three times daily with meals
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥20 mmol/L, then review every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: NG107 sodium bicarbonate for CKD metabolic acidosis

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; eGFR 9.6 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for pain; topical agents if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or GLP‑1 RA if glycaemic control required (once diabetes status confirmed)

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; guideline prohibits dual RAAS blockade
contraindications.alternative: Use single ACE‑I (ramipril) unless intolerant, then switch to ARB

contraindications.reason: Risk of hyperkalaemia in advanced CKD

contraindications.drug: Nephrotoxic antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin) without dose adjustment
contraindications.reason: Drug accumulation and nephrotoxicity at eGFR ≈ 10
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy with eGFR < 30
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with pre‑ and post‑hydration, or alternative imaging modality

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, creatinine, and eGFR trends are assumed stable; will obtain potassium before starting ACE‑I and repeat 1‑2 weeks after each titration.
Liver function tests (ALT/AST, bilirubin) are assumed normal before initiating atorvastatin; will order baseline LFTs.
Hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation are not yet available; ESA and IV iron will be started only after confirming anaemia (Hb <100 g/L) and iron deficiency.
Serum phosphate, calcium, PTH, and bicarbonate values are not provided; phosphate binder, vitamin D analogue, and sodium bicarbonate are conditional on abnormal results.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, iron, sevelamer, alfacalcidol, and bicarbonate is unknown; will verify before prescribing.
Blood pressure reading is not recorded; target BP <130/80 mmHg will be used if proteinuria present, otherwise <140/90 mmHg.
Pregnancy status is not documented; ACE‑I and statin are contraindicated in pregnancy – will confirm patient is not pregnant before initiation.
treatment_summary: The plan initiates renin‑angiotensin blockade with low‑dose ramipril and a moderate‑intensity statin (atorvastatin) as first‑line CKD management per NICE NG203. Conditional therapies address common CKD complications: ESA and IV iron for anaemia, sevelamer for hyperphosphataemia, alfacalcidol for secondary hyperparathyroidism, and sodium bicarbonate for metabolic acidosis, all aligned with NG107. NSAIDs, metformin, dual ACE‑I/ARB, high‑dose potassium, nephrotoxic antibiotics, and unprotected IV contrast are flagged as contraindicated. Monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipid profile, haemoglobin, iron studies, bone‑mineral parameters, and blood pressure is incorporated per guideline recommendations.
